title: Write the first useful email
learningGoal: Make the first reply helpful and human.

items.title: Acknowledge the Enquiry
items.description: Confirm you received their details and express interest in learning more.

items.title: Offer a Clear Next Step
items.description: Provide one way to book a call — a tested calendar booking link.

items.title: Invite Replies
items.description: Let them know they can reply with a question if they are not ready to book.

items.title: Subject: Thanks for getting in touch
items.description: Hi {{contact.first_name}}, Thanks for your enquiry. I have received your details and would be pleased to learn more about what you are working on. If you would like to talk through your goals, you can choose a convenient time here: [Insert your tested calendar booking link]. If you have a question first, simply reply to this email. Best, [Your name]

items.title: Verify Sender Details
items.description: Check sender name, sender address, and merge field preview.

items.title: Test the Booking URL
items.description: Confirm the link opens the intended calendar before using it in a live email.

items.title: Avoid False Claims
items.description: Do not claim you personally reviewed an enquiry if that has not happened.

keyPoint: The first email should acknowledge the enquiry, offer one clear way to book, and invite questions. Always test your booking link and verify sender details before sending.

actionSteps.title: Draft your first email
actionSteps.description: Write a short, helpful email that acknowledges the enquiry and offers a booking link.

actionSteps.title: Test your booking link
actionSteps.description: Click the calendar link to confirm it opens the correct booking page.

actionSteps.title: Preview merge fields
actionSteps.description: Check that {{contact.first_name}} and other merge fields display correctly.

quizzes.question: What is the single action you want the prospect to take after reading the first email?

options.option_text: Book a call or reply with a question

quizzes.explanation: The first email should have one clear call to action: book a call using the calendar link, or reply with a question if they need more information first.

quizzes.question: Why should you test the booking URL before including it in the email?

options.option_text: To make the email look more professional
To confirm it opens the intended calendar and works correctly

quizzes.explanation: Testing the booking URL ensures it opens the correct calendar, the times display properly, and the prospect can actually complete a booking. A broken link defeats the purpose of the follow-up.

quizzes.question: What should you avoid claiming in the first email?

options.option_text: That you personally reviewed their enquiry if you have not
That you would be pleased to learn more
That they can reply with a question

quizzes.explanation: Do not claim you personally reviewed an enquiry if that has not happened. Automated emails should be honest about their nature to maintain trust with the prospect.
